key_insight: A large randomized trial at ICLR 2025 shows that LLM-generated feedback makes peer reviews measurably more informative and increases reviewer–author engagement, demonstrating that model assistance can improve review quality at scale.
problem_solved: Addresses low consistency and limited constructive feedback in peer review by providing scalable, high-quality review guidance to improve informativeness and author interaction.
method: Randomized controlled trial with reviewers at ICLR 2025: reviewers were assigned to receive LLM-generated feedback vs. control.
LLMs produced draft suggestions and comments to augment human reviews; outputs were integrated into the review workflow.
Outcomes measured included review informativeness, quality metrics, and reviewer–author engagement (e.g., replies, revisions).
impact: Shows that LLMs can reliably augment human reviewers to raise review quality and foster better author interaction, offering a practical path to scalable, improved peer review processes for AI/ML communities.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of the randomized trial: assignment → LLM feedback vs control → outcomes
Bar chart comparing average review informativeness/quality between LLM-assisted and control reviewers
Line or stacked chart showing changes in reviewer–author engagement (reply rates, revision actions)
Iconographic before/after: single reviewer vs reviewer+LLM collaboration with checklist of improvements
paper_title: A large-scale randomized study of large language model feedback in peer review
paper_authors: Nitya Thakkar, Mert Yuksekgonul, Jake Silberg, Animesh Garg, Nanyun Peng
